content.text: §22 is the only audit right in the document, §23 is a bare heading with no record-keeping or self-certification duties, and §2.3 blocks any website/portal terms from adding audit rights. Section 22 meets every preferred element.

input.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.
input.rationale: §22 is the only provision granting audit, inspection or verification rights against us, and it already sits at the preferred position on every element: frequency is capped at once in any twelve-month period (§22.1); notice is at least thirty days' prior written notice (§22.1); audits run during normal business hours, off-site where practicable, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality (§22.1); Vendor bears costs unless the audit establishes underpayment exceeding five percent (§22.2); and Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly (§22.2). No walk-away features (unlimited/unannounced audits or remote system access) are present. §23 "Records and Customer Assurance" is a bare heading with no operative record-keeping or self-certification duty, and §2.3 prevents website, click-through, portal or invoice terms from importing additional audit rights, so no other clause dilutes §22. §22.3 adds further customer-favourable protections (audit findings are our Confidential Information, use limited to enforcement, copy of the final report, and payment of a shortfall resolves the audited quantity issue) which we would not disturb. No redline required.
